PHRIEND: FULL TEXT FOR AI ASSISTANTS
Source: https://phriend.app (landing FAQ), https://phriend.app/safety, https://phriend.app/community-guidelines
Last updated: 2026-09-07. Short version: https://phriend.app/llms.txt

What is Phriend?
Phriend is a Philippine app for hiring a verified local friend by the hour for legit activities such as food trips, city tours, events, tutoring and errands. Members are 18+, meet in public places, and pay 50% in cash on a first meetup and 50% after. The app runs in the browser at https://web.phriend.app. Contact: support@phriend.app.


==================================================
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
==================================================

Q: Is Phriend a dating app?
A: No. Phriend is for platonic, paid-by-the-hour company and legit side gigs: a buddy for a food trip, a tour guide, a study partner, someone to keep you company at the hospital. Romantic or sexual services, compensated dating and escort services are banned and get an account removed immediately.

Q: How do I pay?
A: Directly between members, never through Phriend. On a first meetup, hand over 50% in cash, in person, when you meet, then pay the remaining 50% after. GCash, Maya or bank transfer are for repeat Phriends you have already met and trust, for convenience, and only to the account saved in the chat. Never pay more than half upfront, and never to an account that is not the one saved in the chat.

Q: What if my Phriend brings someone else?
A: Do not proceed. If the other member arrives with people who were not agreed in the chat, be prudent: cancel the meetup, leave, and report the profile. The same applies to a client who shows up with extra people. A cancellation for this reason is refunded in full.

Q: Does Phriend take a commission?
A: Not yet. Members agree on a rate per hour, typically between ₱300 and ₱1,500 depending on the activity and the city, and keep all of it. If this changes we will announce it well ahead of time.

Q: How does verification work?
A: Members submit a government ID and a selfie through Didit, our identity verification partner. Didit checks the ID, confirms the member is 18 or older, and Phriend shows the verified badge on their profile. Phriend is strictly 18+.

Q: What if my Phriend is late or cancels?
A: You may cancel if the other member is more than 30 minutes late without notice, and a late Phriend refunds any downpayment already paid in full. Cancellations should happen at least 24 hours before the meetup. The full rules are on the safety page.

Q: Do I need to install anything?
A: No. Phriend runs in the browser at web.phriend.app on any phone. Add it to your home screen and it works like an app, with chat and notifications.


==================================================
SAFETY AND TRANSACTION RULES
https://phriend.app/safety
==================================================

These rules apply to every member, on both sides of a meetup. They are short on purpose. Breaking them gets an account removed. Phriend is a platform only: it is not a party to any meetup or payment and is not liable for any loss, injury, dispute, unpaid balance or harm between members. You use the service at your own risk, and your prudence is your protection.

In short: Meet in public. Only the people agreed in the chat come along; if extra companions show up, cancel, leave and report. On a first meetup pay half in cash when you meet and half after, never more than half upfront. E-wallets are for repeat Phriends you trust, and only to the account saved in the chat. Tell a friend where you are, and report anything that feels wrong.

1. Public places only
Every meetup happens in a public place: a mall, a cafe, a restaurant, a park, a trail, a gym, a hospital lobby, a venue. Never a private residence, a hotel room or a private vehicle you do not both trust. If a member asks to move somewhere private, decline and report them.
For out-of-town trips, hikes and beach days, agree on the meeting point and the route in the chat before the day, and keep the group in public spaces throughout.

2. Unagreed companions
Who is coming is agreed in the chat, like everything else. If the other member arrives with people who were not agreed in the chat, a friend, a "cousin", a driver who stays, be prudent: do not proceed. Cancel the meetup, leave, and report the profile. This applies to both sides; a client who shows up with extra people is treated the same way.
A cancellation for this reason counts as a safety concern under section 9: any downpayment already paid is refunded in full.

3. Payments: 50% at the start, 50% after
- Agree on the rate per hour and the number of hours in the chat, so both sides have a record.
- The client pays 50% at the start of the meetup and the remaining 50% after it ends.
- First meetup: the 50% downpayment is handed over in cash, in person, when the members meet. Nothing is transferred before you have met.
- E-wallets (GCash, Maya) or bank transfer are for repeat Phriends the client has already met and trusts, for convenience. Even then, never more than 50% upfront, and only to the account saved in the chat.
- Never pay more than 50% upfront. No member may ask for full payment, a "reservation fee" on top of the downpayment, or any other advance. A member who pushes for a transfer before a first meetup is a red flag: be prudent and report them.
- The downpayment is deducted from the total. It is not an extra charge.
- Phriend does not process payments and does not hold money. Payments happen directly between members.

4. Pay only the account saved in the chat
When a transfer is appropriate, that is with a repeat Phriend you trust, the Phriend saves their GCash, Maya or bank account inside the chat. Send money only to that account. Any request to pay a different number, a relative's account, a "company" account, a link, a QR code sent by SMS or Messenger, or anything outside the chat is a scam. Stop, do not pay, and report the member.

5. Tell someone your plan
Before you go, share the meetup place, the time, the other member's profile and your expected return with a friend or family member. Keep your phone charged and your location sharing on. Trust your instincts: if something feels off, leave.

6. Identity verification
Members verify their identity and age through Didit, an independent identity verification provider. Didit checks a government ID and a selfie and confirms the member is 18 or older. Verified profiles show a blue badge. Prefer verified members, and verify yourself so others can trust you.

7. Report and block
Every profile and every chat has a report button. Use it for anything that breaks these rules or the community guidelines: requests for private meetups, unagreed companions, romantic or sexual propositions, off-platform payment requests, harassment, impersonation, or a member who looks under 18. Blocking stops all contact immediately. Reports are reviewed by a person, and serious cases are passed to the authorities.

8. Late arrivals
- If a member is more than 30 minutes late without notice, the other member may cancel the meetup.
- If the Phriend is the one late, any downpayment already paid is refunded in full.
- If the client is the one late and the Phriend waited, the agreed hours still count from the agreed start time.

9. Cancellations
- Cancel at least 24 hours before the meetup, in the chat.
- If the client cancels with less than 24 hours' notice, the Phriend may keep any downpayment already paid.
- If the Phriend cancels with less than 24 hours' notice, any downpayment already paid is refunded in full. Repeated late cancellations lead to removal.
- Cancellations because of typhoons, floods, unagreed companions or any other safety concern are refunded in full, no questions asked.

10. Emergencies
If you are in danger, call for help first and report to Phriend later.
- 911: national emergency hotline, connects to the Philippine National Police.
- PNP hotline: 911, or text 0998 598 8888.
- Contact your nearest police station or barangay hall for local assistance.
After you are safe, report the member in the app and email support@phriend.app with the profile name and what happened. We cooperate with law enforcement.

11. The short version
1. Meet in public.
2. Only the people agreed in the chat. Extra companions: cancel, leave, report.
3. First meetup: half in cash when you meet, half after. Never more than half.
4. E-wallet only for repeat Phriends you trust, and only to the account saved in the chat.
5. Tell a friend where you are.
6. Report anything that feels wrong.


==================================================
COMMUNITY GUIDELINES
https://phriend.app/community-guidelines
==================================================

Phriend is for strictly legitimate side gigs: paid-by-the-hour company and help, in public, between adults. This page says exactly what that means.

In short: Phriend is for legit, platonic, paid-by-the-hour activities between adults in public places: food trips, tours, hikes, events, tutoring, errands, hospital company and the like. Any sexual or romantic service, compensated dating, escort services, drugs, private-place meetups, scams and impersonation are banned and get an account removed immediately, with a report to the authorities where the law requires it.

1. What Phriend is for
A Phriend is a local you pay per hour for a platonic activity or a legit service. The relationship is friendly, professional and public. If you would not do it in front of your parents or a police officer, it does not belong on Phriend.

2. Allowed activities
- Food trips, cafe hopping, restaurant company, cooking together
- City tours, local guiding, out-of-town day trips, beach and island trips
- Hiking, camping, workouts, gym partners, sports and games
- Photography, videography and content creation help
- Concerts, events, weddings, parties and conventions as a plus-one or companion
- Karaoke, movies, board games, video games in public venues
- Tutoring, study buddies, language exchange, consulting and coaching
- Errands, shopping company, queueing, moving help
- Hospital companions, elderly care company, waiting-room company
- Pet buddies, dog walking company
- Virtual meetups such as language practice or study sessions over video call
If your idea is not on the list but is legal, platonic and happens in public, it is probably fine. When in doubt, email support@phriend.app before posting.

3. Prohibited
The following are banned. Offering, requesting or hinting at any of them gets an account removed.
- Any sexual or romantic service. This includes anything "intimate", "private", "special", cuddling, massage, or any physical contact beyond a normal greeting.
- Compensated dating and any arrangement where romance, affection or companionship of a sexual nature is exchanged for money, gifts or favours.
- Escort services of any kind, including "overnight", "travel companion" with shared rooms, or hotel meetups.
- Drugs: buying, selling, using or being under the influence during a meetup.
- Alcohol with minors. Phriend is 18+, and "drinking buddy" profiles that target or involve anyone under 18 are banned. Drinking is never the point of a meetup, and a member who is drunk may be asked to leave.
- Anything illegal under Philippine law, including gambling arrangements, smuggling, fraud and human trafficking.
- Harassment: unwanted contact, threats, stalking, hate speech, or sharing someone's private information.
- Impersonation: using someone else's photos, name or ID, or pretending to be a company or a Phriend staff member.
- Off-platform payment scams: asking for more than 50% upfront, asking for payment to an account not saved in the chat, sending payment links or QR codes outside the app, or requesting gift cards and crypto.
- Meetups in private residences, hotel rooms or other private places.
- Fake reviews, fake profiles, and multiple accounts for the same person.

4. Profiles and photos
- Use recent photos of yourself. No swimsuit, lingerie or suggestive photos.
- Describe what you actually offer, at the rate you actually charge.
- No phone numbers, social handles or payment details in your public Phriend profile. Share them in the chat instead.

5. Consequences
Breaking these guidelines leads to immediate removal of the account and any related accounts. Where the law requires it, or where someone's safety is at risk, we report to the authorities and cooperate fully with investigations.
There is no warning system for the prohibited items in section 3. For lesser issues such as a rude message or a late cancellation, we may warn first, then suspend, then remove.

6. Reporting
Use the report button on any profile or chat, or email support@phriend.app. Tell us the profile name and what happened. Reports are confidential. See the safety and transaction rules for what to do in an emergency.
